title: South STL architectural board approves 429 Gley Avenue porch as submitted despite thin-roof concerns

South STL architectural board approves 429 Gley Avenue porch as submitted despite thin-roof concerns
Board members questioned whether the new porch roof framing looked too thin before voting to approve the project without changes.
The South STL architectural review board approved plans for a new front porch stoop at 429 Gley Avenue as submitted, after raising concerns about the thickness of the proposed roof structure.
The meeting took place Thursday, Oct. 1, 2026.
THE CONCERN Board member Tracy said the new porch structure felt thin. "I feel like the the new porch structure feels kind of thin. I don't know what size framing you're using on that, but we have 2x6 roof rafters," she said.
Another board member agreed the renderings made the structure look slim, saying "Yeah, pretty thin," and suggesting a larger board size "just to give it some weight."
THE DESIGNER'S RESPONSE Meg Blaze, with Hercules Design Build, explained the thinner profile was a deliberate choice made with the homeowners. "We uh we reviewed a few options with the client and they preferred the thinner structure," Blaze said, adding that "the house was a depression era house and the thicker structure looked too grand for the front of their house." Blaze noted she had added an inch to the rake board or fascia board since the drawings were plotted, but kept the 2x6 roof rafter.
OTHER QUESTIONS Board members also asked whether renderings distorted the geometry of the porch roof, with one member saying "It's not the geometry looks a little bit different in the renders." Questions were also raised about how the porch roof would interface with the existing soffit and whether an engaged column would overlap window and door trim, which Blaze clarified would not occur.
OUTCOME After discussion, a board member said, "I don't think we have any clarifications or anything," before making a motion to approve 429 Gley Avenue as submitted. The motion passed with one member opposed.
